description: Root React component and entry-point page of the TabCommand UI, mounted at / via React 18 createRoot. Reads uxSettings / labels / activeTabs / allUrls / loadDataSource through the Chrome abstraction and reacts to chrome.storage.onChanged. Renders the sidebar — AppBrand, Settings + ThemeToggle tools, Search, the SearchHint line, the Favorites section, the load-aware Triage card (Home only), and a footer holding the tab/group counts and the Import/Export link, plus the relocated Browser Load gauge whose wrapper is rendered only when hasPerTabLoadData(loadDataSource) holds, so no empty divider hairline is left behind on stable Chrome — alongside a content area that routes between the Home grid (Labels + Tabs under a DragDropContext, persisted via the applyDrag reducer), Load, History, ImportExport, and UrlDetails pages.
name: App

description: Sidebar wordmark: the 4-color TabCommand mark plus a Tab/Command text wordmark in their brand colors. Clicking it returns to Home via the parent-supplied onClick.
name: AppBrand

description: Callback-based storage abstraction faithfully ported from the reference TabCommand. Exposes get(from, keys, callback) / set(from, updates) / remove(from, keys), preserving the leading `from` debug-label arg. Keys are now ROUTED PER AREA underneath that unchanged contract: `labels` lives in chrome.storage.sync so groups survive an uninstall, everything else stays local. A mixed batch fans out and re-merges, and get still invokes its callback exactly once. On get it applies default-hydration once on the merged result (labels/uxSettings/autoClosed -> {}, activeTabs/allUrls/previousLabels -> []) and strips each previousLabels entry's timestamp while dropping falsy entries. The storage contract every feature plan's reads build on.
name: Chrome

description: One draggable section of the sidebar's tab rail: a Droppable wrapping one Draggable Url row per url. It lives at module scope rather than inside Tabs' body because a component declared inside a render is a new type each time, which remounts the Droppable/Draggable subtree and makes @hello-pangea/dnd cancel an in-flight drag.
name: DraggableTabUrls

description: The muted line a page shows in place of its list when there is nothing to show. History and ViewAllFavorites each carried their own copy of this markup off identically-styled classes before it was hoisted here. Takes a message.
name: EmptyState

description: The backup half of the recover/backup page: the current groups serialized to JSON, and every prior snapshot beneath it. The Previous stack is what makes the page a recovery tool rather than a backup button — when a sync warning appears, the user often needs the snapshot from before whatever went wrong. Every snapshot here, current and previous alike, is copyable in one click, because the whole purpose of the page is handing the user a snapshot they can paste somewhere safe; Current reaches that through the same SnapshotField the Previous rows use rather than a second copy control, so the two behave identically. The Previous entries are a list, where a per-row button is the only way to act on a specific row.
name: ExportPanel

description: Renders a url row's favicon with a graceful fallback: the site's image when available, otherwise a deterministic colored monogram tile (via faviconMonogram). Falls back on image load error too.
name: Favicon

description: One favorite on the Favorites View All page: favicon, title, a stats strip that explains the rank (visit count in the window, last-visited via relativeTime, the decay score), and a UsageSparkline of usage over time. A site open in a tab gets the accent open cue; a hidden (removed) favorite is dimmed and shows a Bring back button instead of being filtered out. The whole row opens or focuses the tab on click; onOpen and onBringBack are supplied by the page.
name: FavoriteRow

description: Sidebar section listing the user's genuinely most-visited sites, up to 10 that clear the minimum-visit threshold, ordered by the frequency times recency-decay blend in the pure rankFavorites util so the list reads as favorites over the recent past rather than all-time. Reads allUrls plus the matching url-* records from chrome.storage.local, and also reads activeTabs and favoritesHidden. Suppression is split by what each concern actually means: pinned-tab exclusion is page-level and stays in the excludedKeys set, while user-removed sites go through hiddenSiteKeys into rankFavorites' site-level excludedSites. It also builds an openKeys set of non-pinned active-tab urlKeys so a site currently open in a non-pinned tab has its in-progress visit discounted rather than excluded. A favorite that rankFavorites flags isOpen renders with the Favorites-item--open modifier giving a subtle lime accent-tinted background and left stripe as an already-open cue. Stays live via chrome.storage.onChanged on allUrls / url-* / activeTabs / favoritesHidden. Renders a Favicon plus title per row plus a hover-revealed remove control. That control writes the row's SITE key — derived via hiddenSiteKey, the same normalization the read side and View All's Bring back use — not the representative page's urlKey: a row means the whole host, so storing a page key would hide only that page and the row would immediately re-form from the site's next-most-recent page, which is what forced a user to click the same row once per stored page. Removal hides rather than deletes, so the site stays available in Search and History. On row click focuses an already-open tab or opens a new one. Renders nothing when there are no qualifying favorites.
name: Favorites

description: The Reset favorites tracking control on the Favorites View All page. A quiet utility button at rest; clicking it reveals an inline two-step confirm with a destructive Yes reset everything and a Cancel, so the destructive action takes a deliberate second click. Owns only the confirm/cancel toggle state; the reset itself is onReset, supplied by the page.
name: FavoritesResetControl

description: History page component: composes PageHeader, a HistorySection per day bucket, and EmptyState. All data work — reading the stores, dating each row via historyTimestamp, bucketing, sorting newest-first, staying live, and deleting a row — belongs to the useHistoryRows hook, so this file holds no logic of its own; it passes the hook's reopen and deleteRow straight down. Deleting deliberately leaves group membership untouched, so a deleted page can still appear on its group card and in Search.
name: History

description: One closed/visited tab row in the History list: a group-color dot, the tab favicon (monogram fallback via Favicon), the title with a full title+URL tooltip, a mono timestamp when known, and a HistoryRowActions action pair. The whole row is a click/keyboard target that reopens the tab. Owns only the `confirming` toggle for the two-step delete — it both drives HistoryRowActions and keeps the row visually raised while the second click is pending. The delete path is opt-in: without an onDelete prop the row renders exactly as before, so existing render sites are unaffected.
name: HistoryRow

description: The trailing action area of a History row, in one of two states: at rest a Reopen button plus an optional square delete affordance, and while confirming a red destructive Delete beside a Cancel. Purely presentational — the confirming flag lives in HistoryRow, which also uses it to hold the row visually raised while the second click is pending. Returns a fragment rather than a wrapper so the buttons stay direct flex children of the row and inherit its gap. Every button stops propagation, without which arming or confirming a delete would also fire the row's own click-to-reopen. The delete affordance arms an INLINE confirm rather than a native confirm dialog, following FavoritesResetControl: the confirming state is a real rendered state, so it can be shown, captured and cancelled — a native dialog can be none of those, and is auto-dismissed by the capture browser besides.
name: HistoryRowActions

description: One day group on the History page: the bucket name as a mono eyebrow followed by its HistoryRow list. Renders nothing for an empty bucket so a day with no history leaves no orphan heading. Threads both onReopen and the optional onDelete down to every row. Rows arrive already sorted newest-first from useHistoryRows; this component does not reorder them.
name: HistorySection

description: Local Lucide-style inline-SVG icon set (1.9px stroke, currentColor, round joins) that replaces @ant-design/icons. A name->path lookup returning static SVG; color and size are driven by the caller.
name: Icon

description: The Import / Export page (entry point for Pages.IMPORTEXPORT in App): a recover/backup view reached from the sidebar Import/Export link. Reads labels (sync), previousLabels and syncStatus (local) in ONE cross-area Chrome.get, then composes PageHeader, SyncWarning, ImportPanel and ExportPanel — it owns the storage orchestration and no JSX of its own. Import parses the pasted snapshot through parseImportSnapshot, and a failure is RENDERED rather than logged: the page stays open with the pasted text intact, success is confirmed by reading storage back rather than by the absence of an exception, and an import that needed repair or lost groups reports what happened instead of closing. Only a clean, complete restore calls onComplete.
name: ImportExport

description: What happened to the snapshot the user just pasted. Two tones rather than two components: an import that failed and one that succeeded-but-was-repaired are the same obligation wearing different colors — say what happened, in the same place, in the same shape. A failure is an `alert` because the user must act on it; a repair report is a `status` because it is an account of something already done. Renders nothing without a message, so a caller passes its state straight through without guarding.
name: ImportMessage

description: Where a saved snapshot is pasted back in to restore the user's groups. Purely presentational — the parse, the write, and the read-back confirmation stay on the page, because whether the groups actually landed is a storage question. What it owns is the arrangement: the message sits BETWEEN the box and the button, so an account of what went wrong appears next to the text it went wrong on rather than below the control that triggered it.
name: ImportPanel

description: Global keydown pub/sub over a single document.onkeydown listener: add/remove subscribers and trigger fans an event (real or synthetic) to all of them. Powers Search's Cmd/Ctrl+F focus + Escape close and SearchResults' arrow/enter navigation.
name: KeyDown

description: One group card: a colored title bar (click selects the group via uxSettings.selectedLabel), a 28px menu button opening a LabelCollectionMenu, and a full-card Droppable spanning the title bar and a vertical list of Url rows split into active above inactive. The menu and its click-outside dismiss overlay are portalled to document.body and positioned via anchoredMenuCoords, because the card's own overflow: hidden (load-bearing for the UrlOver inset ring and rounded corners) would otherwise clip the menu at the card's bottom edge. While a tab is dragged the whole card highlights in the group color when it is the cursor target. removeUrl keeps its original meaning — un-file the page from the group and log it via buildGroupRemovalEntry — and then offers an explicit second choice to also delete the page from history, asked only after the group removal and its audit entry are already written so declining never rolls back the un-filing. The card is itself draggable for reordering. It also owns the live preview of an in-flight edit: previewTitle/previewBackgroundColor sit in the same state bag as the committed values and are fed by the menu form's onPreview, deliberately never reaching chrome.storage so a previewed color cannot leak to the real Chrome tab group. groupCardAppearance resolves the pair against the committed values for both the title bar and the --group-color drag-highlight variable, so the drop highlight follows the preview too. toggleMenu clears the preview on both its branches, which is what makes Cancel, the dismiss overlay, and re-clicking ⋮ all revert the card through a single edit. The form is always seeded from the committed color, never a preview, so a cancelled edit reopens clean. onSaved promotes the committed values as it clears the preview, closing the gap in which the card would otherwise repaint the old color before Labels re-keys and remounts it from storage.
name: LabelCollection

description: A group card's ⋮ menu: a LabelForm for renaming/recoloring the group, then a LabelCollectionMenuActions list. Rendered by LabelCollection through a portal to document.body and placed at the viewport coordinates in its `coords` prop, because the group card's own overflow: hidden would otherwise clip it at the card's bottom edge. Takes `menuRef` as a plain prop rather than using forwardRef so the parent can measure the rendered height and correct the placement before paint. Threads the form's onPreview and onSaved callbacks straight through to LabelForm so the card behind can show the pending color and title live; the menu holds no state of its own for either.
name: LabelCollectionMenu

description: The action list at the foot of a group's menu. Renders a single Delete Group action that calls the supplied onDelete. Group sharing has not shipped, so no Share entry is rendered — it is hidden rather than shown disabled, so the menu only offers actions that actually do something.
name: LabelCollectionMenuActions

description: Create/edit form for a label (group): a title input, a swatch picker from Colors, and a LabelFormCustomColor pill that flows as the last item of the swatch grid for picking a non-preset color. The `label` prop is the mode discriminator — present means edit mode (header 'Edit group', submit button 'Save'), absent means create mode (header 'New group', submit button 'Create group'). On submit writes the label into the labels map keyed by title — deriving backgroundColor (Colors[title.length % len]) and position when absent, and deleting the old key on a rename. Two optional callbacks let a host preview the edit before it is committed: onPreview fires from an effect keyed on the DERIVED previewColor and title, so the preset buttons, the custom-color input, and the length-based auto-pick all report through one path rather than per-control wiring, and it fires on mount too (harmlessly — the initial values equal the host's committed ones). onSaved hands back the committed { title, backgroundColor } inside the Chrome.get callback after Chrome.set, so a host can promote the values as it clears its preview instead of repainting the old color for the frames before the storage change re-renders it. Both are optional, so create mode passes neither.
name: LabelForm

description: The collapsible "+ Add Group" affordance at the top of the Labels grid. Toggles an expanded wrapper (with a click-catching #BackgroundOverlay) that hosts a LabelForm for creating a new group.
name: LabelFormContainer

description: The custom-color pill, rendered as the last item of the group form's swatch grid so it flows to the end of the final swatch row rather than claiming a row of its own: a preview dot, the text 'Custom', and a visually hidden native input type=color. Rendered as a label rather than a button because the label wrapping is what forwards a click anywhere in the pill to the input, so the input stays 1px instead of stretching — a stretched color input paints its own swatch over the dot and text. Sized 24px + 1px border to match the 22px + 2px border swatches. The isCustom prop drives the selected border; the dot always shows previewColor, so it doubles as a live preview of the pending color.
name: LabelFormCustomColor

description: A small uppercase section header used inside a group card to demarcate a subset of Url rows. Renders a lime live-status dot, the section label, and a compact count pushed to the right. Purely presentational; the parent decides when to render it.
name: LabelSectionHeader

description: The groups area filling the Home center: reads the labels map + uxSettings from chrome.storage, sorts groups by title then position, pins the selected label expanded above the grid, and chunks the rest into responsive horizontal Droppable rows of LabelCollection. Shows the Add Group CTA when empty.
name: Labels

untestabilityReason.justification: Layout-only stub — renders an empty div with id, no props or logic.

description: The Load page (entry point for the LOAD page in App): composes LoadPerTabNote (shown when per-tab data is unavailable), a list of LoadUrl cards built from activeTabs + the per-URL storage objects, and the raw process table (LoadProcesses), plus a Home link that writes uxSettings.page back to Home. The sidebar LoadMeter gauge links here.
name: Load

description: Sidebar gauge: two concentric SVG arcs (cpu inner, memory outer) whose filled fraction reflects the processTotals storage key, rendered via gradient-path per-segment fill mutation. Reads processTotals on mount and via chrome.storage.onChanged; pure logic is factored into deriveGaugeTotals + gaugeFillPercent. Composes LoadMeterCaption for the source-aware label beneath it. GradientPath calls are guarded to no-op under jsdom; the visual is verified by scenario capture. Clicking it navigates to the Load page.
name: LoadMeter

untestabilityReason.justification: Layout-only stub — renders an empty div, no props or logic.

description: Source-aware label beneath the LoadMeter gauge. Reads the loadDataSource storage marker: system -> a subtle whole-browser-load caption; none -> an explicit No load data indicator (so the empty gauge reads as legible, not broken); processes/unknown -> nothing. Owns its own storage read so the gauge stays purely about the arcs.
name: LoadMeterCaption

description: Honest note on the Load page shown when per-tab CPU/memory is unavailable. Reads loadDataSource: on system/none it explains that per-tab/per-process data needs Chrome Dev channel (chrome.processes) so the empty per-tab bars and process table read as intentional; on processes (or before the marker is known) it renders nothing. Owns its own storage read, sibling of LoadUrl/LoadProcesses.
name: LoadPerTabNote

description: The Load page's raw per-process table: one block per OS process showing task titles plus CPU and private-memory readouts with inline load bars, formatted via humanReadableNumber. Driven by chrome.processes.onUpdatedWithMemory — the live API in a packaged extension; in the codeyam preview the chrome shim emits any seeded `processes` snapshot so the table can be demonstrated (empty when nothing is seeded).
name: LoadProcesses

description: A single card in the Load page's URL list: the tab's favicon (default fallback) and title linked out in a new tab, plus a per-tab load readout (average CPU + private memory with a severity-colored bar via summarizeProcessLoad) when the URL's sampled processes data is present.
name: LoadUrl

description: The shared chrome at the top of a full-page view: a back link, the page title, and an optional one-line intro. History and ViewAllFavorites each rendered this trio inline off the same Page- classes before it was hoisted here. Takes title, intro, onBack and an optional backLabel.
name: PageHeader

description: Sidebar search box: builds a minisearch index over labels and the WHOLE allUrls archive — labeled and unlabeled URLs — with fields labelTitle/urlTitle/url/notes and boosts. Rebuilds on chrome.storage onChanged for a labels change, an allUrls grow or shrink, or a notes edit on any indexed url, re-reading labels and allUrls each time. Typing runs a prefix search; results are deduped and segmented via segmentSearchResults into the SearchResults overlay as labels, grouped urls, and archived urls, each capped at 10. Cmd/Ctrl+F focuses, Escape closes. A build-token guards overlapping async rebuilds. Document shaping is factored into buildSearchDocuments and buildUrlDocuments.
name: Search

untestabilityReason.justification: Layout-only stub — renders an empty div, no props or logic.

description: Static single-line muted hint rendered under the search bar on Home: tells the user they can just start typing to search. No props, no branching, single visual state.
name: SearchHint

untestabilityReason.justification: presentation-only static text, no props or branching, single visual state

description: The search overlay rendered by Search: sections for Groups, Grouped URLs, and Archived URLs. The Grouped URLs section is split into one sub-section per group via groupSearchUrlsByLabel, each headed by the group's color dot and title, with url rows rendered beneath; Archived URLs renders unlabeled hits with the same url row renderer, including a highlighted notes snippet via searchNotesSnippet. Plus a No Results empty state; a section renders only when it has hits. Keyboard navigation with Arrow up/down + Enter and mouse hover move the selection across the flat labels-then-grouped-urls-then-archived list (grouped urls flattened group by group so activation indices stay aligned with render order); activating a label selects it and routes Home, activating a url focuses or opens its tab, and the edit pencil routes to the URL detail page.
name: SearchResults

description: Sidebar gear popover of preferences. Always-visible controls: a Theme Day/Night/System segmented control writing the themePreference storage key [read by useTheme], an Auto-close-after slider, and a Group-columns 2/3/4 segmented control persisted to the settings storage key. The Warn at and Heavy tab >= load sliders render ONLY when per-tab data exists [loadDataSource === processes]; on stable Chrome they hide. The gear sits at the top of the sidebar header, so the panel opens DOWNWARD and is centered on the gear, clamped into the viewport; it is rendered through a portal to document.body so the header transform cannot become the containing block for its fixed positioning [which would break placement and let content paint over it]. Both segmented controls compose the shared SettingsSegment sub-component.
name: Settings

description: Reusable segmented button-group used inside the Settings popover. Presentational only: renders one button per option, marks the active one via aria-pressed, and calls onChange with the value on click. The full flag selects the full-width Theme variant whose segments stretch evenly; omitted it is the inline digit picker. Used by both the Theme Day/Night/System control and the Group-columns control.
name: SettingsSegment

description: The mono text field a snapshot lives in — pasted into for Import, read out of for Export. One component rather than three copies of the same rule, because the Import box, the Current export, and each Previous snapshot are the same object in three roles and have to keep looking identical or the page stops reading as one surface. Read-only is the common case; onKeyDown is passed through rather than assumed because the Import box must stop key events propagating, or the app's type-to-search steals every character of a paste-and-edit.
name: SnapshotBox

description: A read-only snapshot with its own Copy button, which flips to a green Copied for ~1.6s before reverting. Laid out as a row rather than stacked because the Previous list holds several and a button under each box would double the list's height. The clipboard write's rejection is deliberately swallowed — writeText rejects in a headless capture, a hardened profile, or a non-secure context, and unhandled it would surface as a page error on the one path this feature tells users to take when their groups are not reaching sync.
name: SnapshotField

description: The banner telling the user their groups are NOT reaching chrome.storage.sync. Takes a syncStatus record and returns null for the three non-alarming cases — no record, a healthy `ok`, and an unrecognized status from a future version — so it only ever appears when there is something to act on. The copy differs by remedy: an over-quota set needs the user to export and prune, an unavailable sync area needs them to sign in, and it names the consequence in the user's terms rather than the mechanism. Two optional props let the same component stand away from the Import / Export page: onOpenBackup switches the copy to point AT that page (rather than saying 'below', where the snapshot is not) and adds the button to get there, and onDismiss adds the close affordance a banner needs when it sits above the user's groups on Home rather than on a page they chose to open.
name: SyncWarning

description: Home tab list: renders Active Tabs, Automatically Closed, and collapsible History sections from chrome.storage; splits tabs into label groups vs an ungrouped remainder; filters browser-pinned tabs and expired auto-closed entries. Each row is a draggable Url.
name: Tabs

description: Sidebar light/dark toggle button: shows the moon glyph in light mode (click switches to dark) and the sun glyph in dark mode (click switches to light). Theme and toggle handler are owned by the parent.
name: ThemeToggle

description: Sidebar load-triage card (Home only) whose color tracks overall load vs settings.warnAt: red 'Running hot' with a 'Review N heavy tabs' CTA, amber 'Getting busy', or green 'Comfortable'. Counts heavy tabs (per-tab load >= heavyThreshold) and toggles the shared review mode. Renders ONLY when per-tab data exists (loadDataSource === 'processes'); hidden on stable Chrome (system/none/unknown), and the red high state is suppressed when no culprit tab crosses the threshold (heavyCount === 0). Pure load->level math is in loadLevel.
name: Triage

description: A single tab/url row: shows favicon + title (derived from urlKey when untitled), a process-load indicator (level + bar width from averaged CPU/memory), and a hover action row (pin/keep-open, edit, delete, close) wired to chrome.tabs and Chrome storage. Its remove action routes through the shared deleteUrlFromHistory and only THEN closes the tab — the previous order (close first, remove the url record ahead of the allUrls splice) is what let the service worker's onRemoved handler read a pre-delete snapshot and resurrect the row at the top of History.
name: Url

description: The URL Details page (entry point for Pages.URL in App): the full-screen form to edit one saved URL — title/url/favicon inputs, a notes textarea, and removable Groups chips for its label memberships. Reads the per-URL object + labels from Chrome storage. On Save: an unchanged URL key updates in place; a changed URL re-keys the record (writes under the new url-key, migrates its allUrls position and every label membership, removes the old key) — akin to delete-old, add-new — and stamps edited so the tracker keeps the curated title/favicon. Then returns Home; Cancel returns Home. Composes UrlField and UrlLabel; pure logic lives in utils/urlDetails.
name: UrlDetails

description: A single labeled field in the UrlDetails edit form — an <input> (Title/Url/Favicon) or, with `multiline`, a <textarea> (Notes). Reproduces the onKeyDown stopPropagation guard that keeps the app's global Esc/Search key handlers from firing while typing. Class is derived from the field name (UrlDetails-form-<name>).
name: UrlField

description: One removable 'Groups' chip in the UrlDetails form: a close icon plus the label title, with the title passed as the button value so the page handler knows which group to remove. Clicking it asks the page to drop this URL from that group.
name: UrlLabel

description: Two inline bar charts side by side on a FavoriteRow: usage over the last SPARK_DAYS days (recent daily rhythm) and the last SPARK_WEEKS weeks (longer-term trend that varies in height even when daily usage is steady). Built from bucketVisitsByDay and bucketVisitsByWeek, no charting library. An optional common `max` prop lets the page scale every row's bars to one shared maximum so heights are comparable across rows; without it each chart self-scales to its own busiest bucket. Visited buckets are tinted the brand accent.
name: UsageSparkline

description: The Favorites View All page: a full-page, uncapped list of every qualifying favorite ranked by decayed score, each rendered as a FavoriteRow showing its title, its URL as a clickable open control, rank-explaining stats, and a usage sparkline. Reads allUrls, activeTabs, and favoritesHidden from storage in an effect and stays live via chrome.storage.onChanged, calling rankFavorites with an Infinity limit and a site-level hiddenSites set built from hiddenSiteKeys, so a removed site renders dimmed with a Bring back action no matter which of its pages is currently the representative — flagging by page key would leave a multi-page site's row undimmed and its Bring back unreachable. Bring back is the exact inverse of the sidebar's remove: it clears EVERY favoritesHidden entry that normalizes to the row's site key, legacy url-* page entries included, so one click fully restores the site. Removing only the matching entry would leave the site's other entries behind, so it would stay hidden despite the click and, with no dimmed row left to click, be permanently stuck that way. Includes a FavoritesResetControl that clears the visit signal (visits/visitCount) and favoritesHidden so the favorites list starts over, leaving History and Search intact. Mirrors the History page shell and focuses an already-open tab on click or opens a new one. Reached from the sidebar Favorites section View All link.
name: ViewAllFavorites

description: Viewport coordinates for a menu or panel anchored to a button, for menus rendered through a portal with position: fixed to escape an ancestor's overflow: hidden. Right-aligns the menu to the anchor's right edge, clamps it horizontally inside the viewport, and flips it above the anchor when there is no room below — a control low in a scrolling grid would otherwise open its menu off the bottom of the screen. A menu taller than the space above still starts on screen. Margin and gap are tunable; rect is any object with top/bottom/right, so callers pass a real getBoundingClientRect and tests pass a literal.
name: anchoredMenuCoords

description: Pure ring-buffer helper for the grouping diagnostics trail: appends one breadcrumb to the current stored array and returns a new array trimmed to the most-recent cap entries, treating a missing or non-array store as empty and never mutating its input. Kept free of chrome/IO so it is unit-testable in isolation.
name: appendGroupingLog

description: Pure reducer behind App's onDragEnd. For URL drops it moves a urlKey out of the source label and into the destination label, translating the drop index from the card's DISPLAYED order (open tabs first, via labelDisplayOrder) onto the stored urlKeys order before splicing -- so a row lands where it was dropped rather than at the displayed index's stored position. An index at or past the end appends. Reports the active tab ids to ungroup when a url leaves an active label. For LABEL_COLLECTION drops it reorders groups by rewriting each label's position. Returns null when there is no destination, or when the destination group no longer exists.
name: applyDrag

description: Resolves which chrome.storage area owns a key, defaulting anything unknown to local. `labels` is the sole sync entry — it is the irreplaceable record of the user's groups, and Chrome destroys the local area on uninstall (including the implicit uninstall when an unpacked extension's directory goes missing) while the sync area is restored from the user's Google account. The unbounded dynamic `url-<url>` records default to local because they would blow the 102,400-byte sync area quota.
name: areaForKey

description: The line a permissive parse must not cross: returns the parsed value as an importable label list, or null when it is not an export. Keeps the valid labels and counts the dropped ones so a partial document still restores what it can while reporting what it could not. An EMPTY array is rejected rather than imported, because it is indistinguishable from garbage that happened to parse and importing it would clear every group the user currently has.
name: asLabelList

description: Maps a process's task tab ids back to tabs (chrome.tabs.get) and merges per-url process metrics into the updates object.
name: associateProcess

description: The Closer engine sweep: reads activeTabs/autoClosed/settings, prunes stale entries, then closes every eligible inactive tab via chrome.tabs.remove and records each into the autoClosed map so the Automatically Closed UI updates.
name: autoCloseSweep

description: Resolves the active inactivity threshold in minutes from settings.autoCloseMinutes, falling back to the default when unset and returning 0 when the user has set the Off position.
name: autoCloseThresholdMinutes

description: Reads the close time out of an autoClosed entry in either stored shape — the bare numeric epoch the service worker writes today, or the legacy object form carrying time and backgroundColor. Returns null for anything else. Covered by historyTimestamp's object-form test.
name: autoClosedTime

description: Navigates from the History page back to the Home page by updating uxSettings.page via Chrome storage.
name: back

description: Module-level navigation helper for the ViewAllFavorites page: resets uxSettings.page to Pages.HOME via the Chrome storage wrapper so the back button returns to the Home view. Mirrors the History page's back helper.
name: back

description: Buckets a closed/visited tab timestamp (ms epoch) into the History page day groups — Today, Yesterday, or Earlier this week — relative to a passed-in now. A missing timestamp falls into Earlier this week so the tab still appears. Exports HISTORY_BUCKETS for render order.
name: bucketByDay

description: Splits the tabs bound for one label into per-window buckets so each window resolves its own Chrome group. chrome.tabGroups.query is not window-scoped, so a title-only query can return a group living in another window, and chrome.tabs.group against that group physically drags the tab across windows — the cross-window pull this fixes. A label legitimately has one Chrome group per window. Drops pinned tabs, which matters beyond tidiness: a bucket holding only pinned tabs would otherwise cause an empty Chrome group to be created for that window. Entries persisted by a build predating the windowId field bucket under undefined, where the caller falls back to the unscoped query until updateActiveTabs rewrites them.
name: bucketTabsByWindow

description: Pure helper that buckets a site's visit timestamps into per-day counts over a trailing window of SPARK_DAYS days, oldest day first, relative to now. Visits older than the window or in the future are ignored. The Favorites View All page feeds the result to the UsageSparkline so a user sees a site's usage-over-time at a glance and understands why it ranks where it does.
name: bucketVisitsByDay

description: Pure helper that buckets a site's visit timestamps into per-week counts over a trailing window of SPARK_WEEKS weeks, oldest week first, relative to now. Each bucket spans 7 days and aggregates the visits within it, so the Favorites View All page's long-range sparkline varies in height even when daily usage is a steady one-per-day. Visits older than the window or in the future are ignored. Companion to bucketVisitsByDay for the short-range 7-day view.
name: bucketVisitsByWeek

description: Builds one entry for the always-on group-membership ADDITION audit trail, the mirror image of buildGroupRemovalEntry. Coerces urlKeys to an array, normalizes a missing tabId to null while preserving tabId 0, carries `total` as the label's member count AFTER the add, and carries `previousKey` only for the drift-heal source where the add is a rewrite-in-place. Clock-free: `t` is caller-supplied so the builder stays pure and needs no chrome or Date stubbing. Exists because groups were growing members nobody filed and no trail recorded which code path appended them.
name: buildGroupAdditionEntry

description: Builds one entry for the always-on tab MOVE audit trail — the third sibling of buildGroupAdditionEntry and buildGroupRemovalEntry. Those two trail label membership; neither records the thing users actually notice, which is the tab jumping position in the strip, so a report about tabs moving was undiagnosable without this. Records the source path, whether the call was a group or ungroup, the tab, and the group ids before and after, so a move is readable at a glance. Missing group ids default to -1 and missing label or urlKey normalize to null, keeping serialized entries a stable shape. Kept clock-free — t is caller-supplied — so it is unit-testable without stubbing chrome or Date. Only calls actually issued are recorded, so a placement suppressed by the tabPlacement guards leaves no entry and a quiet steady state reads as an empty trail rather than a guess.
name: buildGroupMoveEntry

description: Pure builder for one always-on group-membership removal audit entry. Given a removal source tag and details, returns a uniform record carrying the caller-supplied timestamp t, source, label title, a urlKeys array coerced from a bare key or array, a tabId normalized to null when absent while preserving a real 0, and the label's remaining member count after the removal. Clock-free and IO-free so both runtimes build identical breadcrumbs and it is unit-testable without stubbing chrome or Date.
name: buildGroupRemovalEntry

description: Builds the storage updates map from an export: one per-URL object per url-<url> key plus the rebuilt labels map. Accepts either the raw pasted JSON string or an already-parsed, already-validated label list. The page passes the second form, because reading a snapshot a transport medium damaged is a whole escalation ladder rather than one JSON.parse, and because the shape has to be validated BEFORE anything is written.
name: buildImportUpdates

description: Builds the cumulative ladder of repair candidates for a pasted snapshot — the untouched paste at index 0, then each successive transport repair applied on top of the last. Because the caller attempts a parse after each rung, the repair set eventually reported to the user is the SMALLEST one that actually worked rather than everything that could have been applied.
name: buildRepairCandidates

description: Turns the stored labels map into the synchronous half of the Search index: one minisearch document per label (id 'label-<title>' with color), a labelMap of every labeled urlKey to its label title, and a labelColorMap of every label title to its color. Its companion buildUrlDocuments stamps each grouped URL document with urlLabelColor (from labelColorMap) alongside urlLabelTitle, so grouped hits can be headed by their group's color downstream. Pure, so index shaping is testable independent of minisearch/Chrome.
name: buildSearchDocuments

description: Builds one minisearch document per URL across the WHOLE archive — the deduped union of allUrls and labeled keys — from the per-URL storage records. urlTitle falls back to url; urlLabelTitle is set only for labeled keys and left undefined for archived URLs, which is the signal used downstream to bucket archived hits. Keys with no backing record, and duplicate keys, are skipped so a partially-seeded store never throws and minisearch is never double-added.
name: buildUrlDocuments

description: Builds the per-URL object persisted on Save from the UrlDetails form fields: always title/url/favicon plus edited:true (marking the record user-curated so the tab tracker stops overwriting title/favicon), plus notes only when non-empty. DROPS the per-URL processes object. Extracted from the page handleSubmit.
name: buildUrlInfo

description: Returns the change entry a storage.onChanged event carries for a key, but only when the event's areaName matches that key's OWN area. Exists because the two areas fire separately: one event carries only one area's keys, so the pre-split `if (areaName !== 'local') return` preamble silently dropped every labels change once labels moved to sync. Centralizing the gate means the service worker, LabelCollection, Search, Labels, Tabs, and App cannot drift apart on it. The last three were missed by the original conversion sweep, and the gap was not cosmetic: with the grid (Labels) deaf to every labels change, deleting a group wrote storage correctly and left its card on screen — the whole user-visible 'Delete Group does nothing' symptom — while the sidebar kept the group's heading and the footer kept its count. Recolor and rename hid the bug because LabelCollection repaints its own card from its own listener; deleting is the one mutation that needs the PARENT to re-render.
name: changedInArea

description: Clamps a number to the [0, 1] range, used to normalize CPU/memory ratios before rendering the load gauge.
name: clamp01

description: Moves a closed tab's url key to the front of `allUrls`, persists the reordered list, and invokes an optional callback. Returns early WITHOUT writing in two cases, both of which would otherwise corrupt history. First, a key that is not tracked: an absent key yields indexOf -1, and splicing at -1 removes the LAST element, which would silently promote the OLDEST key to the front and corrupt the recency order the tail-eviction in newUrl depends on. Second, a key carrying a `deletedUrls` tombstone: the page was just deleted from History in the popup process, but this handler runs off chrome.tabs.onRemoved in the service worker holding a pre-delete snapshot, so the move-to-front would write the deleted key straight back at index 0 — resurrecting the row, titleless, because its url record was already removed. Skipping costs nothing since closeUrl only ever REORDERS an existing key. Both early-return paths still invoke the callback, because onRemoved passes updateActiveTabs.
name: closeUrl

description: Vite plugin for the query-param component-isolation stack: exposes the codeyam-generated components and component-scenarios artifacts as codeyam:components / codeyam:component-scenarios virtual ES modules (returning a valid empty module before first generation), resolves codeyam:isolate to the on-disk .codeyam/harness/isolate.jsx so Vite transforms it as real JSX (throwing loud if missing), and invalidates the virtual modules when .codeyam/generated changes.
name: codeyamPlugin

description: Returns the de-duplicated list of urlKeys across the sorted labels — the exact set the Import/Export page hands to Chrome.get to resolve each per-URL object before serializing the export.
name: collectUrlKeys

description: Maps a viewport width in pixels to the most group columns the center pane can comfortably fit, using the widest-first COLUMN_BREAKPOINTS, returning 1 below the narrowest breakpoint. Used by effectiveColumns to cap the user's chosen count responsively.
name: columnsForWidth

description: Whether a viewport point falls inside an element's bounding rect, on both axes. Module-private to dropTargeting, where dropTargetAtPoint uses it to decide whether the cursor is over a card's rows region at all -- a point outside it, over the title bar or the slack below the last row, is an ambiguous drop that appends rather than resolving to a row slot. Exercised through dropTargetAtPoint's tests.
name: containsPoint

description: Copies one relative path from the scratch build directory into the stable extension mirror, creating parent directories as needed.
name: copyFile

untestabilityReason.justification: A two-call fs.mkdir/fs.copyFile boundary with no branching.

description: Internal helper of deriveSystemTotals: average per-core busy fraction = delta(kernel+user)/delta(total) across processors between two chrome.system.cpu samples. Returns 0 (never NaN) for missing/empty/single-sample input and for a non-advancing counter.
name: cpuUtilization

description: Builds the chrome shim object backed by in-memory stores for BOTH storage areas, hydrated from window.localStorage (codeyam's seed inlet). Each seeded key lands in the area that owns it, so existing scenarios seed unchanged; the `sync::` / `local::` prefixes override that to make the cross-area states seedable — sync populated with local wiped, and local populated with sync empty. Serves storage.local and storage.sync get/set/remove/clear with localStorage mirroring (JSON string boundary kept inside the shim) and onChanged dispatch carrying the correct areaName, plus callable no-op tabs/tabGroups/processes/runtime action stubs so interactive preview scenarios never throw on missing chrome APIs.
name: createChromeShim

description: Durable, runtime-toggleable diagnostic recorder for the tab-grouping decision points. Optionally emits a TC-GROUP console line when the compile-time DEBUG_GROUPING is on, and persists each breadcrumb to a capped groupingLog ring buffer in chrome.storage.local when the runtime debugGrouping flag is set, so grouping decisions survive MV3 service-worker restarts and are inspectable after the fact. Fire-and-forget: the storage round-trip never blocks the caller.
name: debugGroup

description: Pure helper that scores a site as the sum of its visits' exponentially-decayed weights, each 2 to the power of negative age over halfLifeMs, so a fresh visit is worth 1.0 and a visit one half-life old is worth 0.5. A future-dated timestamp from clock skew is clamped to weight 1. Returns 0 for empty or non-array input. This is the core ranking signal for Favorites: recent visits count more than old ones, and a site clears qualification when its summed decayed score reaches QUALIFY_MIN.
name: decayedVisitScore

description: The local-to-sync migration decision as a pure function of both areas' current values, returning the outcome, the labels the session should run with, and whether a copy is owed. Sync wins whenever it holds groups (the second-machine case), local is copied up when sync is empty (the upgrade path), and an over-quota map is left local rather than written to fail. Pure so the decision table is testable without stubbing chrome.
name: decideMigration

description: Internal shim helper: invokes a callback asynchronously on a microtask (Promise.resolve().then) with an optional value, matching Chrome's async callback contract so consumers never depend on synchronous delivery. No-ops when no callback is supplied.
name: defer

description: The single place a page is deleted from History, shared by the History row's delete action, the group card's also-delete-from-history path, and Url's remove action. In one read-modify-write it splices the urlKey out of allUrls, drops its autoClosed entry, and writes a deletedUrls tombstone, all in a single Chrome.set — and only then removes the url record, because removing the record while the key was still listed is what made a resurrected row render as a bare titleless URL. The tombstone is what the service worker's closeUrl consults, closing the cross-process race where an in-flight tabs.onRemoved holding a pre-delete allUrls snapshot wrote the key back at index 0. Guards indexOf -1 so deleting an untracked key cannot splice away an unrelated page, and always invokes its optional callback.
name: deleteUrlFromHistory

description: Returns the label titles a `labels` write REMOVED — present in the previous map, absent from the next — which is exactly the set of groups the user just deleted and the trigger for dissolving their Chrome tab groups. Pure and area-agnostic so the worker's storage.onChanged listener keeps no set-difference logic of its own and the case can be tested without stubbing chrome.* at all. Both sides tolerate null/undefined: `newValue` is undefined when the key is removed wholesale, which is what deleting the LAST remaining group does, and coercing it to an empty map is what makes that case report the deletion instead of silently reporting nothing. Presence is keyed on the key rather than on truthiness, so a label whose value is falsy is not mistaken for a deleted one.
name: deletedLabelTitles

description: Maps a stored processTotals record onto the two values the LoadMeter gauge renders: cpu (inner arc) and memory (outer arc, the sum of privateMemory + jsMemoryUsed bytes). Every field is optional so a partial or empty record reads as zero, never NaN. Factored out of LoadMeter's storage handler so the data binding is unit-testable independent of the SVG.
name: deriveGaugeTotals

description: Pure stable-Chrome fallback math for the LoadMeter gauge: turns two chrome.system.cpu samples plus a chrome.system.memory reading into a processTotals-shaped record normalized to the gauge's 0->max scale (cpu = avg per-core busy fraction * max.cpu; privateMemory = base + memory-pressure ratio * max.memory; base cancels so gauge fill == utilization). All fields guarded so empty/single-sample inputs read as zero, never NaN. Mirrors deriveGaugeTotals/gaugeFillPercent; fed by the service worker's pollSystemLoad.
name: deriveSystemTotals

description: Derives the UrlDetails 'Groups' chip titles from the labels map + a urlKey: the title of every label whose urlKeys contains that urlKey. The chips are derived state, never stored. Extracted from the page's setPartialState so it can be unit-tested in isolation.
name: deriveUrlLabels

description: Describes the destination-group addition caused by a URL drag, or null when nothing joined a group: non-URL drags (label reorders), drops outside any group, drags with no destination, and same-group reorders. Mirror of describeDragRemoval, but deliberately DOES describe a sidebar-origin drag — that drop adds a member while removing none, which is exactly the 'where did that row come from' case the addition trail exists for. The returned shape feeds straight into buildGroupAdditionEntry as its details object.
name: describeDragAddition

description: Pure descriptor of the source-group member removal caused by a URL drag, or null when nothing should be recorded: non-URL label reorders, sidebar-origin drags with no source group, drags with no destination, and same-group reorders. Parses the @hello-pangea/dnd result to name the source label and moved urlKey, and reads the post-applyDrag labels map for the source group's new length. Its return shape feeds directly into buildGroupRemovalEntry as the details object.
name: describeDragRemoval

description: The one-line account of an import that succeeded but was not intact, and null for a clean one. Silent repair would leave a user believing a damaged backup is healthy, and silent PARTIAL recovery is worse still because it looks exactly like a complete restore — so the repairs are named and the lost count is stated plainly. Omits the salvage label when groups were lost, since the count sentence already accounts for that damage and naming it twice reads as two separate problems.
name: describeImport

description: Dissolves the Chrome tab groups belonging to labels the user just deleted, so no tab survives in a titled group to re-record the label that was removed. Tabs stay open and stay put — chrome.tabs.ungroup only clears membership and never reorders tabs or moves them between windows — so this is a deliberate, user-initiated exception to the no-autonomous-tab-moving guarantee rather than a regression of it. Queries unscoped by window and handles EVERY returned group, since a label legitimately has one Chrome group per window and the deletion removes all of them. Each affected tab is added to pendingUngroups BEFORE the call lands, reusing the record loop's existing in-flight guard to close the window in which a concurrent groupTabs pass would re-record it, and cleared in the callback. A deleted label with no live Chrome group is the common case (its tabs are all closed) and is a silent no-op. Every ungroup is trailed through recordMove under MoveSource.WORKER_LABEL_DELETED.
name: dissolveDeletedLabelGroups

description: Resolves both the group under the cursor and the slot within it as a droppableId plus index, or null when the point is over no group card. The index counts the rows whose vertical midpoint the cursor has passed, excluding the dragged row's own floating clone, and is an index into the card's DISPLAYED order so applyDrag translates it onto stored order. A point outside the rows region -- the title bar, the empty state, the slack below the last row -- is an ambiguous drop and appends rather than landing at the top. Runs during pointer tracking because onDragEnd carries no coordinates and the drop animation has already returned rows to flow by the time it fires.
name: dropTargetAtPoint

description: Resolves the group droppableId under a viewport point via elementFromPoint, so a dragged tab targets whichever group the cursor is over instead of @hello-pangea/dnd's center-based collision. Returns null when the point is over no group card.
name: dropTargetIdAtPoint

description: Walks up from a DOM element to its enclosing group-card drop zone and returns that zone's @hello-pangea/dnd droppableId, or null when the element is not inside a group card. Backs cursor-based drop targeting.
name: dropTargetIdFromElement

description: Computes the column count the groups grid should render: the user's configured count from settings, capped by what the current viewport width can comfortably fit, floored at 1. Falls back to ColumnsDefault for missing or invalid input. Drives the chunk size and the --label-columns card-width variable in Labels.
name: effectiveColumns

description: Pulls a Chrome-auto-inherited tab back out of the group it was born into rather than making its URL sticky. Defers while the URL is unloaded, re-reads labels from fresh storage to avoid an ungroup-then-regroup flicker when the URL is genuinely a member, otherwise ungroups via pendingUngroups and clears the auto-group flag. Returns wait, kept, or ejected.
name: ejectAutoGroupedTab

description: Synthetic event factory: returns an event-shaped object with no-op stopPropagation/preventDefault spread with the given attributes, so code can feed a synthetic key into KeyDown.trigger (e.g. SearchResults triggering Escape after a click).
name: event

untestabilityReason.justification: synthetic event factory — object literal spread with no branching

description: Derives a deterministic favicon fallback monogram for a url row: the first visible letter (scheme/www. stripped, title preferred, '?' when empty) and a palette color chosen by hashing the url, so the same site always gets the same tile.
name: faviconMonogram

description: Resolves which label claims a urlKey, returning the first matching label title or null. The single source of truth for the question two callers ask and must not answer differently: groupTabs picking an ungrouped tab's destination group, and updateActiveTabs testing membership before ejecting a revisited auto-closed tab. Returning the FIRST match is the anti-flip-flop guarantee — the previous loop queued a tab into every label claiming its urlKey, so a URL filed under two labels was grouped twice in one pass, into group A and then group B, with the winner depending on async tabGroups.query ordering and therefore able to differ pass to pass. First-by-Object.keys order is an arbitrary choice of label but a stable one, and stability is the property that stops the alternation. Null-tolerant on both arguments and skips malformed label records so one bad entry cannot break grouping for the rest.
name: findLabelForUrlKey

description: Coerces one timestamp candidate to a finite epoch-ms number, or null. Mirrors the Number.isFinite guarding pruneVisits uses so strings, NaN and undefined fall out rather than poisoning the Math.max that historyTimestamp takes over its candidates. Covered by historyTimestamp's junk-input tests.
name: finite

description: Whether an item is small enough to write to chrome.storage.sync under an enforced 7KB margin below Chrome's 8,192-byte QUOTA_BYTES_PER_ITEM. Measuring before the write means an oversized labels map is redirected to local deliberately, rather than discovered as a runtime error whose swallowing would leave the user's groups silently un-backed-up while the UI still showed them.
name: fitsSyncItemQuota

description: Formats the auto-close inactivity threshold in minutes for the Settings control, rendering Off for non-positive values, whole minutes under an hour, or hours with a single decimal only when not whole.
name: formatAutoClose

description: Pure fill math for the LoadMeter gauge, factored out of the SVG-mutation effect so it is testable without a DOM. Given a measured value, the arc base floor and max ceiling, returns the percent of segments that stay EMPTY (100 - filledFraction*100); a fuller gauge returns a smaller number. Intentionally un-clamped to mirror the reference.
name: gaugeFillPercent

description: Reads whether a drag is currently in flight. Lists call it to decide whether to apply an incoming storage update or buffer it until the drag ends, since re-rendering mid-drag cancels the drag.
name: getDragActive

description: Reads the current cursor drop-hover state from the external drag-hover store.
name: getDragHover

description: Promise/callback hybrid read across BOTH storage areas, handing back one merged result: invokes the callback when supplied, otherwise resolves with the result. Renamed from getLocalStorage because it is no longer local-only — `labels` comes from chrome.storage.sync while everything alongside it in the same query (activeTabs, allUrls, the url-* records) comes from local.
name: getStorage

description: Thin promise wrapper around chrome.system.cpu.getInfo() so pollSystemLoad can await it uniformly. Platform boundary to the Chrome system API.
name: getSystemCpuInfo

untestabilityReason.justification: Direct chrome.system.cpu API call; exercised indirectly through pollSystemLoad with a mocked chrome.system.

description: Thin promise wrapper around chrome.system.memory.getInfo() so pollSystemLoad can await it uniformly. Platform boundary to the Chrome system API.
name: getSystemMemoryInfo

untestabilityReason.justification: Direct chrome.system.memory API call; exercised indirectly through pollSystemLoad with a mocked chrome.system.

description: Promise wrapper around chrome.tabGroups.get that resolves null for absent/sentinel (-1) group ids.
name: getTabGroup

description: Derives a stable storage key for a URL by stripping the hash fragment and prefixing `url-`.
name: getUrlKey

description: UI-side twin of the service worker getUrlKey: derives the storage key url-<url-without-#hash> for a URL. Codified in one reusable place so the UrlDetails re-key logic on Save mirrors the service worker canonical keying rule.
name: getUrlKey

description: What a group card should paint right now: the pending appearance an open edit form reported through onPreview when one is in flight, otherwise the committed values. Returns color and titleText. The two fallback chains carry the whole preview contract — LabelCollection clears the preview fields to null on every dismissal path, so dropping them is what reverts the card and there is no separate revert step; and titleText falls through to the committed title rather than the empty string, so clearing the name field mid-edit previews as the current title instead of a blank header. Returns an undefined color when neither a pending nor a committed color exists, leaving the neutral default to the caller rather than inventing one. Takes a plain object so the fallbacks are unit-testable without mounting the card, its portal, its Droppable, and chrome.storage.
name: groupCardAppearance

description: Pure helper that turns the flat list of grouped-URL search hits into an ordered set of per-group sub-sections for the SearchResults overlay. Each hit carries urlLabelTitle and urlLabelColor; this collapses them into an array of {title, color, urls} where groups appear in first-appearance order and urls keep their input order within a group. A null, empty, or non-array input yields an empty array. Kept free of React so the grouping is unit-testable; consumers flatten the groups to recover the flat activation order that stays aligned with render order.
name: groupSearchUrlsByLabel

description: Reconciles Chrome tab groups against the labels model: groups labeled tabs (creating/coloring groups as needed) and ungroups tabs that no longer belong to any label, skipping pinned tabs. Refuses to record a tab whose ungroup is in flight (in pendingUngroups) so a tab navigating out of a group is never captured into it. Also stamps the label slot each tab occupies on both paths that CONFIRM membership rather than create it -- the urlKeyIsMember branch for an in-group tab, and the urlKeys-match branch for an ungrouped tab about to be auto-added -- because the append guard reads only that stamp, and clicking a URL already filed in a group appends nothing and so never triggers the create-time stamps. Persists every stamp from a pass in ONE conditional activeTabs write after the loop; the condition is load-bearing, since an unconditional write would re-enter onChanged and loop forever.
name: groupTabs

description: Diffs old vs new activeTabs to reconcile label membership when a tab moves between groups, adding/removing its url key from the affected labels; seeds a missing destination label instead of throwing, skips tabs whose ungroup is pending, and no-ops without a previous value. Only group-to-group moves reach the append site -- it bails when either the old or new group fails to resolve, so an ungroup-to-nothing never arrives -- and that append now also carries the navigatedAwayFromRecordedSlot guard, so a tab still stamped under the destination label that navigated and was moved back in does not contribute its live url as a second phantom member. The old-group removal below is unguarded, so a genuine re-home into a DIFFERENT label still moves the member.
name: handleActiveTabsGroupChanges

description: Whether a labels map is a non-empty object. The distinction is the migration's whole correctness argument: {} is the hydrated empty default, so treating it as authoritative would let an empty sync area permanently shadow a populated local one and the user's groups would appear to vanish.
name: hasGroups

description: Predicate over the loadDataSource storage marker: true only for the 'processes' source, which is the sole source that attributes CPU and memory to individual tabs. Stable Chrome reports 'system'/'none', and the marker is absent before the service worker writes it. Shared by LoadMeter, Triage, Settings, LoadPerTabNote and App's sidebar-footer gauge wrapper so all five per-tab surfaces hide and show on exactly the same condition. Distinct from loadLevel, which bands an already-known load percentage rather than deciding whether per-tab load is knowable at all.
name: hasPerTabLoadData

description: Heals a group label slot whose recorded urlKey has drifted from a tab live URL - as Google Docs rewrites its own ?tab= query. Locates the slot for the same page by samePageKey, then rewrites it in place to the live key or splices it out when the live key already exists elsewhere, never adding a new slot. Returns found/mutated/previousKey plus a removed flag that is true only on the dedup splice branch, so callers can audit a genuine member drop while ignoring a harmless in-place rewrite. Shared by the onUpdated navigation heal and the recordInGroupTab grouping-sync path so a drifted doc keeps its position instead of dropping to the bottom of the group.
name: healDriftedLabelSlot

description: Normalizes ONE stored `favoritesHidden` entry to the site key it hides: strip a leading `url-` to recover the raw URL, then reduce it via `siteKey(url) || normalizeUrl(url)` — the same expression `rankFavorites` builds its group keys with. Exported alongside the set-building `hiddenSiteKeys` so the WRITE side spells `which site is this row` exactly as the READ side does. That matters because a lone `siteKey` call is wrong here: a bare hostname is not a parseable URL, so `siteKey('espn.com')` returns '' — precisely the form site-level removal now writes. The `normalizeUrl` fallback is what hands such an entry back unchanged, making it load-bearing rather than merely defensive. Both the sidebar's remove (deriving the key to store) and View All's Bring back (testing which stored entries belong to a row's site) go through this function, so a legacy `url-` page entry and a fresh bare site key resolve identically and write/read cannot drift apart. Returns '' for anything it cannot normalize; callers treat '' as no site and skip it.
name: hiddenSiteKey

description: The read-side bridge for the `favoritesHidden` store, which can hold two forms at once: LEGACY page keys (`url-<url>`) written before favorite removal became site-level, and the bare SITE keys written from now on. `hiddenSiteKeys(list)` normalizes a whole stored list into a Set of site keys; the exported singular `hiddenSiteKey(entry)` normalizes one. Both strip a leading `url-` to recover the raw URL and then reduce it via `siteKey(url) || normalizeUrl(url)` — deliberately the SAME expression `rankFavorites` derives its group keys with, so the hidden set and the group keys it is matched against agree by construction rather than by coincidence. That fallback is load-bearing rather than merely defensive: a bare hostname is not a parseable URL, so `siteKey` alone returns '' for exactly the form removal now writes, and `normalizeUrl` is what hands it back unchanged. A legacy page entry therefore keeps hiding its whole site with NO storage migration and no version bump. Junk that normalizes to nothing is dropped instead of being added as an empty key that could collide with a malformed group key, and a missing or non-array input yields an empty set so callers can pass unvalidated storage straight through. All three call sites — the sidebar's remove, the sidebar's exclusion set, and View All's Bring back — derive `which site is this row` through this one module, so write and read cannot drift apart.
name: hiddenSiteKeys

description: Derives the timestamp a History row displays and buckets by: the most recent thing that happened to a URL, taken as the max of the url record's lastVisit, the newest entry in its visits array, and its autoClosed time in either the bare-number or legacy object form. Returns null only when nothing is known, leaving bucketByDay's Earlier this week fallback as the honest answer. Pure and Number.isFinite-guarded, so junk in any input is skipped rather than poisoning the max. Replaces reading autoClosed alone, which left every manually-closed or still-open page undated.
name: historyTimestamp

description: Formats a numeric value with locale-aware thousands separators for the Load page's raw per-process table (1284 -> '1,284'). A falsy value yields undefined so the caller renders nothing; locale defaults to the document language then 'en', overridable via the lang arg. Factored out of the Load page so the formatting is unit-testable.
name: humanReadableNumber

description: Applies the Chrome abstraction's default-hydration rules — labels/uxSettings/autoClosed to {}, activeTabs/allUrls/previousLabels to [], theme to dark, settings to the load tunables — plus the previousLabels timestamp strip and falsy-entry drop. Extracted so the rules run exactly ONCE on the merged cross-area result and behave identically whether a read touched one area or both.
name: hydrateDefaults

description: Popup entry point: focuses the existing pinned TabCommand app tab if open, otherwise creates one at index 0, then closes the popup.
name: init

description: Channel-based degradation entry point for the Browser Load gauge, run at worker load. Uses chrome.processes when present (Dev/Canary, full per-tab fidelity, processProcesses tags loadDataSource 'processes'); else falls back to chrome.system.* polling ('system'); else writes loadDataSource 'none' so the UI can say there is no load data.
name: initLoadSource

description: Installs the in-app chrome shim on globalThis only when the real extension chrome.storage.local is absent (inert in a packaged extension, so production behavior is unchanged). Replaces the reference App.jsx's sinon-chrome fallback; called once at src/index.jsx before the first render. Returns true when it installed the shim, false when a real chrome was present.
name: installChromeShim

description: Predicate deciding whether an activeTabs entry may be auto-closed: not Chrome-pinned, not tabCommandPinned, not the active tab, and last active at or before the cutoff.
name: isAutoCloseEligible

description: Service-worker mirror of the src/lib/utils/isSearchEngineUrl predicate: returns true when a URL host (via the local siteKey mirror) is a known search engine - a curated exact-host set plus a google.<tld> ccTLD rule. Used by newUrl to skip the Favorites scoring writes (per-record visits + the durable siteVisits host bucket) for search engines, which rankFavorites discards anyway. Duplicated here because the service-worker runtime cannot import the ES module, matching the siteKey and pruneVisits mirroring convention; SEARCH_ENGINE_HOSTS is kept byte-identical to the canonical set.
name: isSearchEngineUrl

description: Pure predicate returning true when a URL points at a known search engine. Reduces the URL to its canonical host via siteKey, then tests it against a curated exact-host set of engines and SERP subdomains plus a google.<tld> ccTLD rule. Whole-host matching so an already-inflated siteVisits row disappears immediately, while distinct Google hosts like docs.google.com stay favoritable. Shared by rankFavorites - which drops search hosts before grouping so they never qualify as Favorites - and a byte-identical mirror in service_worker.js. Returns false for non-string, empty, or unparseable input.
name: isSearchEngineUrl

description: Pure predicate deciding whether a URL is a real website worth recording into history/Favorites. Returns true only when the value is a non-empty string that parses as a URL whose protocol is exactly http: or https:; returns false for non-strings, empty/whitespace, unparseable values, and every other scheme such as about: including about:blank, file:, data:, view-source:, chrome:, chrome-extension:, devtools:, blob:. One rule replaces an ever-growing blocklist. Imported by the service worker's newUrl to gate what enters allUrls, and by rankFavorites to defensively drop already-stored non-website entries. Complements validTab which is tab-shaped and worker-only; this predicate is URL-shaped and stack-agnostic, mirroring the defensive try/new URL/catch style of normalizeUrl.
name: isTrackableUrl

description: Joins the named repairs into a readable phrase rather than a comma-separated dump, so a snapshot that needed several fixes reads as a sentence. The message it feeds is the only account the user gets of what was wrong with their backup, which is exactly why it should not read like debug output.
name: joinPhrases

description: Orders a group's urlKeys the way its card paints them: open tabs first, saved-only rows after, preserving stored order within each section via a stable sort. The single definition of that rule, shared by LabelCollection's render and the drag reducer's display-to-storage index translation so the two can never drift apart. Tolerates a null urlKeys or activeTabs, and never mutates the array it is given.
name: labelDisplayOrder

description: Internal shim helper: resolves the callback argument from a variadic action-stub call by returning the last argument when it is a function, else undefined. Lets the no-op tabs/tabGroups stubs accept Chrome's varying (props, cb?) / (id, props, cb?) arities.
name: lastCallback

description: Returns the newest finite timestamp in a url record's visits array, or null for an absent, empty or all-garbage array. The signal that dates a page visited today but never auto-closed. Covered by historyTimestamp's latest-visit and junk-input tests.
name: latestVisit

description: Recursively lists every file under a directory as paths relative to it, returning an empty list when the directory is absent. Used on both sides of the mirror: to enumerate what the build produced and what the target still holds.
name: listFiles

untestabilityReason.justification: A bare fs.readdir recursion whose entire work is the filesystem call; it carries no decision of its own, since the ordering and pruning rules live in the separately-tested orderedSyncPlan and staleFiles.

description: Subscribes processProcesses to chrome.processes.onUpdatedWithMemory, guarded by try/catch so a missing processes API (non-Chrome / no permission) degrades quietly.
name: listenToProcesses

description: Maps a load-bar width percentage to a CSS color variable (high >= 70, medium >= 40, otherwise light).
name: loadColor

description: Maps an overall browser-load percentage onto the three triage/gauge severity bands (low/medium/high) given the user warnAt threshold; the medium band begins at warnAt*0.6. Shared by the LoadMeter gauge and the Triage panel so both color the same load identically. Distinct from summarizeProcessLoad which yields a per-tab level.
name: loadLevel

description: Entry point for the extension-directory mirror: copies the built output into dist/extension in orderedSyncPlan order, then prunes what the build no longer produces. Exists because Vite builds with emptyOutDir, so build/ is deleted and recreated on every run — and if Chrome reads the directory it has loaded while it is missing, it treats the extension as uninstalled and destroys its chrome.storage.local with it, which is the incident this feature exists to prevent.
name: main

untestabilityReason.justification: Build-time orchestration of filesystem I/O and process exit; its two real rules are extracted into orderedSyncPlan and staleFiles, both unit-tested, and the end-to-end guarantee is confirmed by running npm run build.

description: Bidirectional Chrome group-color map: converts a named tab-group color to its hex value and vice versa. Lifted to module scope so both groupTabs and handleActiveTabsGroupChanges can color a seeded label.
name: mapColors

description: Finds the brace closing the object that starts at a given index, or -1 when the text runs out first — which IS the truncation signal salvage keys off. String-aware, so a brace inside a page title cannot throw off the depth count and truncate a perfectly good group.
name: matchingBrace

description: Internal helper of deriveSystemTotals: system memory pressure = (capacity - availableCapacity)/capacity, clamped 0..1. Returns 0 (never NaN) when the info object or capacity is missing.
name: memoryUtilization

description: Reads both storage areas, applies decideMigration, performs the copy when owed, and hands back the resolved labels. Runs on service-worker boot AND on app boot — MV3 recycles the worker constantly, so a not-yet-migrated user who opened the full-page app first would read labels from an empty sync area and see zero groups. Idempotent, so both entry points running it is safe. Deliberately one-way-safe: the local value is LEFT IN PLACE as a read-only fallback, never deleted, so a sync failure degrades to the old behavior instead of losing data.
name: migrateLabelsToSync

description: The localStorage key a shim write mirrors back to — the inverse of resolveSeedKey, so a value round-trips into the area it was written to. A key in its natural area mirrors unprefixed (keeping the seed format stable); a key written to the OTHER area, like the labels local fallback after a quota rejection, mirrors prefixed so the next boot does not hydrate it as if it were the synced copy.
name: mirrorKeyFor

description: Whether a tab is the one already filed under a slot in a label and is now sitting on a different url — a navigation, not a new member. The precise, per-tab, exact-key test behind the phantom-member fix: a path change is not a same-page drift, so healDriftedLabelSlot finds no slot and the grouping sync used to append the live url as a second permanent member, one per navigation the eject path missed. Deliberately not per-title or per-host, since a group legitimately holds several pages of one site. Requires the recorded slot to still be a live member so a stale stamp cannot suppress genuine appends forever.
name: navigatedAwayFromRecordedSlot

description: Idempotence guard answering whether a tab genuinely needs a chrome.tabs.group call to reach a target group. False when the tab is pinned or already sits in the target group, because chrome.tabs.group is a REPOSITION rather than an assertion: Chrome honors it even when the tab is already there, appending it to the end of the group. That unguarded re-assert is both a visible tab move and a self-sustaining loop, since the move fires onMoved which drives updateActiveTabs, a storage.local.set, storage.onChanged and another groupTabs pass. Filtering placement calls through this predicate is what lets a steady-state pass issue zero Chrome calls and damps the cycle. An absent or -1 target means no Chrome group exists for the label yet and one is about to be created, so every unpinned tab needs the call. Compares group ids against -1 explicitly rather than by truthiness, so group id 0 is treated as the valid group it is.
name: needsGroupCall

description: Idempotence guard answering whether a tab genuinely needs a chrome.tabs.ungroup call. False when the tab is already in no group, because ungrouping an ungrouped tab still repositions it in the tab strip — one of the paths behind users reporting that their tabs move while they do nothing. Applied at every worker ungroup site so a suppressed no-op never reaches Chrome and never lands in the move trail. Treats a missing or null group id as no group, but compares against -1 explicitly so group id 0 stays ungroupable.
name: needsUngroupCall

description: Registers a newly-visited URL and returns the storage updates. Maintains `allUrls` as a true LRU: the url key is MOVED TO THE FRONT on every visit, not merely inserted when absent, so the list genuinely means recency — the ordering the tail-eviction and every consumer already assume. Keys past MAX_TRACKED_URLS (500) are evicted from the tail and their non-labeled records deleted. A real visit also UN-FORGETS a deleted page: it clears the url's `deletedUrls` tombstone and prunes expired tombstones via pruneDeletedUrls on the same pass, so deleting from History means forget-this rather than block-this and the tombstone map stays bounded by DELETED_URL_TTL_MS. Records the visit twice: on the url-* record (visitCount plus a pruned `visits` array, kept for History and backward compatibility) and, durably, under the site's host in the `siteVisits` map, which the eviction branch never touches — so evicting a url-* key can no longer destroy a site's visit history, and every page of a content site credits the site rather than minting an orphan record. All writes land in one storage set. Gated to real websites via isTrackableUrl; no-ops without a tabId/url.
name: newUrl

description: Normalizes a tab's group id so a missing or null value reads as Chrome's TAB_GROUP_ID_NONE. Shared by needsGroupCall and needsUngroupCall so both placement predicates agree on what no group means. Its real job is what it deliberately does NOT do: collapse 0 into no group.
