Group id 0 is falsy but a perfectly valid Chrome group id, and the service worker's older `activeTab.groupId && activeTab.groupId > -1` test mishandles exactly that case — a tab in group 0 would be re-grouped on every pass, or refuse to be ungrouped. Comparing against -1 explicitly instead of by truthiness is what keeps the guards correct at that edge.
name: normalizeGroupId

description: Turns non-breaking and zero-width characters into ordinary spaces or drops them. These are the cruel ones: they are invisible, so a user looking at the rejected text can see nothing wrong with it and has no way to guess what to fix. The zero-width set is matched as an alternation rather than a character class, because a class holding the zero-width joiner is exactly the construct that silently splits an emoji sequence in a page title.
name: normalizeInvisibleCharacters

description: Normalizes a single export entry, or returns null when it is not a label at all. The rules come straight from what buildImportUpdates requires — it keys the labels map by title and iterates urls — so an entry missing either would silently produce a partial map rather than an error. Permissive WITHIN a recoverable label: an unusable member row is dropped rather than the whole group discarded, and a group with no members is kept because an empty group the user made still belongs in their backup.
name: normalizeLabel

description: Pure URL-normalization helper that produces a canonical grouping key for de-duplicating cosmetic URL variants. Collapses the scheme so http and https are equivalent, lowercases the host and strips a leading www., strips a trailing slash from the path, and drops the fragment, while PRESERVING the query so genuinely different pages stay distinct. Its host derivation is delegated to siteKey so that host canonicalization — lowercasing and www.-stripping — has exactly one definition shared with the site-level siteVisits store. Falls back to the trimmed raw string for a non-parseable input so callers never throw on a key-derived or malformed value. Now used by rankFavorites only as a fallback grouping key for candidates whose URL yields no site key.
name: normalizeUrl

description: Reorders the built file list so every asset is copied before manifest.json. A directory holding a manifest IS an installed extension to Chrome, so writing the manifest first would briefly advertise an extension whose code has not landed. Pure and never adds or drops an entry, so the mirror cannot silently drift from the build.
name: orderedSyncPlan

description: Reads a pasted export snapshot as forgivingly as it can be read, escalating through four passes rather than failing: strict JSON.parse, transport-damage repair, relaxed hand-edited syntax, then structural salvage of whatever survives a truncated file. Returns the recovered labels plus the minimal set of repairs that worked, or a typed failure. Validates the SHAPE after parsing so a permissive parse never becomes a permissive import, and on total failure reports the ORIGINAL strict-parse error rather than an offset into a repaired copy that does not exist in what the user pasted.
name: parseImportSnapshot

description: Extracts the integer Chrome tab id from a `tab-<n>` storage key.
name: parseTabId

description: Splits a chrome.storage read query into one query per owning area, preserving the caller's argument form — string, array, defaults-object, or null for everything. Lets a mixed read like Chrome.get(['labels','previousLabels']) fan out and re-merge instead of silently returning half its keys.
name: partitionKeysByArea

description: Splits a chrome.storage write map into one map per owning area, emitting only non-empty areas so a local-only write still costs exactly one round trip. The case that forces it: buildImportUpdates returns url-* records and labels in ONE map, and a naive per-area switch would drop half of every import.
name: partitionUpdatesByArea

description: Scales a value within a [base, max] window to a clamped 0-100 percentage for the triage load bands.
name: pct

description: One stable-Chrome sampling pass: reads chrome.system.cpu + chrome.system.memory, feeds the previous + current sample through deriveSystemTotals, and persists { processTotals, loadDataSource: 'system' }. On any thrown system call it degrades to loadDataSource 'none' and stops polling rather than crashing the worker.
name: pollSystemLoad

description: chrome.processes update handler (Dev/Canary): aggregates per-process CPU/network/memory totals and associates them with tabs, tags loadDataSource 'processes', persists the result, and after ~10 samples pauses listening for 15s to throttle.
name: processProcesses

description: Detects whether the Dev/Canary-only chrome.processes.onUpdatedWithMemory API is present, so the worker can choose the full-fidelity per-tab load path over the stable-Chrome system fallback.
name: processesApiAvailable

description: Removes auto-closed entries older than the retention window from the autoClosed map in place so the Automatically Closed list does not grow unbounded.
name: pruneAutoClosed

description: Drops deletedUrls tombstones older than a ttl, returning a new map without mutating the input. A tombstone only needs to outlive an in-flight tabs.onRemoved to closeUrl that holds a pre-delete allUrls snapshot, so nothing is remembered for long; without pruning the map would accumulate one entry per page ever deleted and grow without bound. The ttl boundary is inclusive, and an entry whose timestamp is missing or non-numeric is treated as expired so a corrupt write cannot pin a key out of history permanently. Called by newUrl on the same pass that prunes allUrls.
name: pruneDeletedUrls

description: Removes empty subdirectories left behind by pruning. The passed directory itself is never a removal candidate — only its descendants — which is what guarantees the mirror root Chrome has loaded always survives a rebuild.
name: pruneEmptyDirs

untestabilityReason.justification: An fs.readdir/fs.rmdir recursion at the filesystem boundary; the invariant it protects (the mirror root survives) is verified against the real filesystem by rebuilding and confirming the directory inode is unchanged.

description: Deletes the files staleFiles identified from the mirror, then tidies up empty directories. The decision of WHAT is stale is delegated to the tested pure helper; this is the removal boundary only.
name: pruneStale

untestabilityReason.justification: A bare fs.rm loop over paths chosen by the separately-tested staleFiles; it owns no selection logic of its own.

description: Service-worker mirror of the visitDecay pruneVisits helper: drops visit timestamps older than VISIT_RETENTION_MS (30 days), filters non-finite entries, sorts ascending, and caps to the newest MAX_VISITS (50). Applied on each newUrl write so per-site visit history recorded for Favorites time-decay ranking stays bounded. Duplicated here because the service-worker runtime cannot import the ES module, matching the GAUGE and AUTO_CLOSE constant-mirroring convention.
name: pruneVisits

description: Pure helper that bounds a per-site visit-timestamp array: it coerces entries to numbers, drops any older than the VISIT_RETENTION_MS horizon or non-finite, sorts the survivors ascending, and caps the result to the newest MAX_VISITS. Keeps stored visit history bounded on write in the service worker and normalizes visits before scoring in rankFavorites. Tolerates undefined or garbage input by returning an empty array. The service worker mirrors this logic because it cannot import the ES module.
name: pruneVisits

description: Whether a partitioned read query asks for `labels` at all. `labels` routes to sync, so the sync side of the partition is the one interrogated, and the `null` read-everything form counts as asking for it. This is the gate that keeps the local-fallback resolution off the hot path: the ~20 reads that never touch `labels` must not pay for a second round trip just because one key in the routing table has a fallback.
name: queryRequestsLabels

description: Pure ranking for the Favorites sidebar and View All page. Candidates are rolled up BY SITE via siteKey — the host — rather than per page, so a content site's homepage and its articles become ONE row whose count and sparkline reflect the site's real usage; the row's representative is the most-recent, lowest-index member. This subsumes the old cosmetic-variant collapsing, since http/https/www variants share a host. A group's timestamps are the deduped UNION of the durable `siteVisits[host]` history and the per-record visits its members carry via visitsFor, which preserves the legacy visitCount migration path; union rather than either-or, because right after the upgrade the durable store holds one timestamp while legacy records hold the site's whole history. Both stores record the same visit with the same epoch-ms, so duplicates collapse. SCORING is time-decayed: a currently-open non-pinned tab is discounted by dropping the site's most-recent in-progress visit — applied AFTER the union, so the durable store cannot hand the dropped visit back — sites below qualifyMin are dropped, and survivors sort by decayed score with recency then list position as tiebreaks. SUPPRESSION comes in two levels that must not be confused. The page-level `excludedKeys` / `hiddenKeys` match a member's `urlKey` and serve the genuinely page-level concern of pinned-tab exclusion. The site-level `excludedSites` / `hiddenSites` match a GROUP's key in the qualifying loop: `excludedSites` drops the whole site, `hiddenSites` flags it `isHidden: true` for View All's dimmed Bring back row. Removal is site-level because ROWS are site-level — suppressing a single page key of a multi-page site only demotes the representative, and the row instantly re-forms from that site's next-most-recent page, which is the bug that forced a user to click the same row once per stored page. Callers build the site sets with hiddenSiteKeys, whose normalization mirrors this function's own `siteKey(url) || normalizeUrl(url)` group key.
name: rankFavorites

description: Reads keys from whichever areas own them and hands the MERGED result to the callback exactly once. The single-callback contract is load-bearing: the Import / Export page reads labels (sync) and previousLabels plus syncStatus (local) in one call and would render twice with partial data otherwise. `labels` gets one extra step — writeByArea redirects it to the LOCAL area whenever sync refuses the write, so resolving it from sync alone made that fallback WRITE-ONLY and the user watched their groups revert. When sync offers no groups, local is consulted for a fallback copy before the callback fires; precedence is decided by resolveLabelsAcrossAreas, and the second round trip is only paid on the degraded path. Degrades to a local-only read when the host exposes no sync area.
name: readByArea

description: Returns a new labels map where every label containing oldUrlKey has it replaced by newUrlKey, position preserved, de-duplicating when newUrlKey is already present. Pure and non-mutating; mirrors the service worker label drift-healing. Used when an edited URL re-keys a record so its group memberships follow.
name: reassignUrlKeyInLabels

description: Records a visit when a tab is activated (switched to), throttled per site to ACCESS_THROTTLE_MS. Resolves the activated tab, ignores untrackable/missing tabs, and only counts the access as a visit when the sites most recent visit is older than the throttle window, otherwise the open-then-activate sequence and alt-tabbing would double-count. Delegates the write to newUrl so access-visits and open-visits stay identical in shape.
name: recordAccess

description: Records a group-membership addition to the always-on groupAdditionLog trail — the mirror of recordRemoval, and unconditional for the same reason. Reads the existing ring buffer, appends a buildGroupAdditionEntry via the shared appendGroupingLog, and writes back under the dedicated groupAdditionLog key so it is never buried by or trimmed with the noisy debugGrouping breadcrumbs. Fire-and-forget: the async storage round-trip never blocks the caller and it only records additions, never changing grouping behavior. Called from every append site with a distinct AdditionSource tag so a phantom member is provable rather than inferred.
name: recordAddition

description: Records one move-trail entry per tab actually handed to chrome.tabs.group. Both grouping branches — creating a new Chrome group for a label in a window, and adding to an existing one — need the identical loop, and a single batched Chrome call moves every tab in it, so the trail records per tab rather than per call and a multi-tab group call stays legible as the several moves it really is.
name: recordGroupMoves

description: Records an in-group tab's URL into its group's label, seeding the label with the group's mapped color when it does not exist yet, then persists via update. Runs only for non-auto-grouped tabs such as startup sync of pre-existing Chrome groups. The final write is now CONDITIONAL on an actual mutation, and the activeTabs membership stamp is written independently of the labels map — the common path (clicking a URL already filed in the group) stamps without mutating labels, and re-persisting an unchanged labels map would burn the sync area's 120-writes-per-minute budget.
name: recordInGroupTab

description: Always-on writer for the tab-move audit trail, the third sibling of recordAddition and recordRemoval and unconditional for the same reason. Reads the current groupMoveLog, appends a buildGroupMoveEntry through the shared appendGroupingLog ring buffer capped at GROUP_MOVE_LOG_CAP, and persists it under its own groupMoveLog key so it is never buried by or trimmed with the noisy debugGrouping breadcrumbs. Called only after the needsGroupCall / needsUngroupCall guards pass, so the trail records real movement and never a suppressed no-op. Fire-and-forget: the async round-trip never blocks the caller and only records moves, never changing placement behavior. The write cannot re-enter the grouping loop because storage.onChanged bails unless labels or activeTabs changed, and this touches neither.
name: recordMove

description: Always-on writer for the group-membership removal audit trail in the service worker. Unlike debugGroup it is never gated by DEBUG_GROUPING or debugGrouping: it reads the current groupRemovalLog, appends a buildGroupRemovalEntry breadcrumb via the appendGroupingLog ring buffer capped at GROUP_REMOVAL_LOG_CAP, and persists it under the dedicated groupRemovalLog key. Fire-and-forget storage round-trip that only records removals and never changes removal behavior, so the next unexplained drop is captured with no flag to pre-enable.
name: recordRemoval

description: Persists the outcome of the most recent sync write under the local-area syncStatus key, but only when the status actually CHANGES. The memo matters because labels is written on every ordinary group edit, so recording unconditionally would turn one diagnostic key into a write on every mutation — the same churn the worker's coalescing guard exists to prevent.
name: recordSyncStatus

description: Pure formatter that maps an epoch-ms timestamp to a compact how-long-ago label relative to a caller-supplied now: sub-hour reads as just now, under a day as N hours ago, under two weeks as N days ago, and beyond as N weeks ago. A missing timestamp reads as never, and a future timestamp is clamped to just now. Used by the Favorites View All page for each favorite's last-visited stat.
name: relativeTime

description: Rewrites the JSON a human hand-edited into strict JSON, then drops trailing commas. Reports `changed: false` for text that was already strict so the caller can skip a redundant re-parse rather than reporting a repair that never happened.
name: relaxSyntax

description: Removes keys from whichever areas own them, routing the same way reads and writes do so a Chrome.remove spanning both areas clears both.
name: removeByArea

description: Returns a new labels map with a urlKey spliced out of the named label's urlKeys (fresh array, input not mutated; unknown label returns the map unchanged). Backs the UrlDetails Groups-chip removal. Extracted from the page's handleLabelClick.
name: removeUrlFromLabel

description: Clears the module-level status memo so each test case starts from a known state. Exported for tests only; production never needs to forget the last recorded sync status.
name: resetSyncStatusMemo

description: Resolves a Chrome group id to its label title, preferring the in-memory groups map and falling back to chrome.tabGroups.get. The fallback is not an optimization detail: right after an MV3 service-worker restart that map is cold, and both onUpdated branches needing a title — the navigation-eject membership check and the in-page drift heal — run in exactly that window. Extracted because those two branches of the same conditional had resolved the title with duplicated inline code.
name: resolveGroupTitle

description: Attaches each label's resolved urls array (url/title/favicon, plus notes only when present) from the per-URL info map and drops urlKeys, returning the labels ready to JSON.stringify into the export. A urlKey with NO per-URL record is expected rather than exceptional now that labels lives in sync while the url-* records stay local: after an uninstall restores the groups, the local records they point at are gone. The URL is reconstructed from the urlKey itself. Dereferencing the missing record previously threw and took down the whole Export panel, leaving the user no way to back up the groups they had just recovered; skipping the member would be worse still, since the export would look complete while silently dropping URLs from the backup.
name: resolveLabelUrls

description: Decides which copy of `labels` wins when the local and sync areas disagree. Sync is authoritative whenever it actually holds groups — it is the copy that survives an uninstall, the entire reason labels moved there — and a local value wins only when sync has none, because it exists solely as the landing site for a refused sync write. Expressed through the same `hasGroups` predicate `decideMigration` applies, so an empty map is treated as the hydrated default rather than an authoritative answer and an empty sync area can never permanently shadow a populated local one. Returns a `{source, labels}` decision so the caller can tell NEITHER apart from 'local won with an empty map'.
name: resolveLabelsAcrossAreas

description: Splits a raw localStorage seed key into the area that owns it and the key the app sees. Unprefixed keys route through the storage-areas table, so every pre-existing scenario seeds unchanged; the `sync::` and `local::` prefixes override that, which is what makes the cross-area states seedable at all — sync populated with local wiped (the uninstall a user survives) and local populated with sync empty (the state the migration converts).
name: resolveSeedKey

description: Rewrites relaxed JSON into strict JSON: line and block comments dropped, single-quoted strings requoted with inner double quotes escaped, unquoted keys quoted, and the non-JSON literals NaN / Infinity / undefined turned into null. Every rule applies only OUTSIDE a string literal, so a page title containing a URL with a double slash or an apostrophe is copied through verbatim rather than mistaken for syntax. Hand-rolled rather than pulled from a JSON5 dependency because this is a browser extension and the tolerated set is small and fixed.
name: rewriteRelaxedSyntax

description: The last resort for a snapshot truncated mid-copy: scans for every well-formed label object still readable and returns those plus a count of what was lost, rather than failing whole. Steps INSIDE an object that parsed but is not a label, so an export nested in a wrapper is still recovered. The lost count is what makes a partial restore honest — a silent partial recovery looks exactly like a complete one.
name: salvageLabels

description: Reduces a URL to its origin + pathname so the tab-grouping eject path can tell an in-page URL rewrite (query/hash change — keep grouped) apart from a real navigation (different origin/path — eject). Drops the query string and fragment; falls back to the raw input for non-string or unparseable values so they compare equal only when literally identical.
name: samePageKey

description: Computes the truncated, highlighted notes snippet under a URL search result whose match landed in its notes: finds the term case-insensitively, captures the original-cased match, windows ~18 chars before / ~24 after, and returns { before, match, after } (or null when there's nothing to highlight).
name: searchNotesSnippet

description: Pure migration helper that synthesizes a recent visit history for a legacy url record that has a visitCount but no visits array. It returns up to MAX_VISITS timestamps spread evenly across the last few days ending at now, so a pre-upgrade favorite keeps a sensible decayed rank on first load instead of vanishing, then converges to real timestamps as the user revisits. A zero or missing count yields an empty array; a count of one yields a single visit at now. This is a one-time, non-destructive approximation applied lazily at score time.
name: seedVisitsFromCount

description: Shapes raw minisearch hits for the SearchResults overlay: dedupes hits by document id, then splits them into { labels, urls, archived } — a hit is a label when it carries labelTitle, a grouped url when it carries urlLabelTitle, and an archived url otherwise.
name: segmentSearchResults

description: Measures a key plus its JSON encoding in UTF-8 bytes, the way chrome.storage.sync counts its quota. UTF-8 rather than String.length because group titles are user-supplied and routinely non-ASCII — an emoji title undercounts by up to 3x under UTF-16 code units, which would let an over-quota write through to fail at runtime.
name: serializedByteLength

description: Sets the drag-in-flight flag for the whole drag lifecycle, including keyboard drags and group reorders. No-ops when the value is unchanged, and never clobbers the cursor-hover state, which is owned by pointer tracking instead.
name: setDragActive

description: Updates the cursor drop-hover state and notifies subscribers, deduping identical updates so group cards only repaint when the hovered target changes. Kept outside React state so updating it mid-drag does not re-render the dragged tab's subtree and cancel the drag.
name: setDragHover

description: Service-worker mirror of the siteKey helper in src/lib/utils/siteKey.js, which is the source of truth: returns a URL's canonical host, lowercased with a leading www. stripped, or an empty string when the URL is unparseable. Used by newUrl to pick the bucket in the durable siteVisits store each visit accumulates into. Duplicated here because the service-worker runtime cannot import the ES module, matching the pruneVisits mirror and the GAUGE and AUTO_CLOSE constant-mirroring convention.
name: siteKey

description: Pure helper returning the canonical SITE key for a URL: its host, lowercased, with a leading www. stripped and no scheme, path, query or fragment. This is the key the durable siteVisits store accumulates visits under and the key rankFavorites groups candidates by, so every page of a content site credits the site itself rather than minting an orphan per-page record. Collapses scheme, host case, leading www. and any path/query/fragment; keeps non-www subdomains distinct, since a subdomain is usually a genuinely different site. Returns an empty string for non-string or non-parseable input so callers can treat it as no site and skip it. normalizeUrl derives its host from this helper so www.-stripping has exactly one definition, and the service worker mirrors it because it cannot import the ES module.
name: siteKey

description: Sorts a labels map into the canonical export order: by title (locale compare) then by position, defaulting a missing position to 0. The two chained sorts mirror the reference ImportExport sortAndStuff.
name: sortLabels

description: Replaces raw newlines and tabs INSIDE string literals with the space they displaced, leaving them alone outside a string where they are legal JSON whitespace. This is the confirmed real-world failure: a user's snapshot was hard-wrapped by the medium they pasted it through, putting a literal newline exactly where a space belongs in a page title, and JSON.parse rejected it with a bad-control-character error the user never saw. A CRLF pair collapses to one space because it replaced one space.
name: spaceOutControlCharacters

description: The target files the new build no longer produces — a set difference over relative paths. Extracted and pinned by tests because it is the one place a bug would DELETE a file the loaded extension still needs; hashed asset names change every build, so pruning has to happen, but it has to prune only what is genuinely gone.
name: staleFiles

description: Stamps an activeTabs entry with the label slot its url was filed under or confirmed as occupying (labelTitle / labelUrlKey), which is the sole input to the navigatedAwayFromRecordedSlot append guard. Lives on the persisted activeTabs entry rather than a module-level Map because MV3 tears the worker down constantly and the post-teardown sync is exactly the window where the bogus append happens, so an in-memory map would be empty precisely when needed; activeTabs entries also vanish when the tab closes, so cleanup is free. Returns whether the stamp actually CHANGED, not a constant true: groupTabs stamps on every pass and persists via a bare storage.local.set that re-enters onChanged and calls groupTabs again, so a caller on that hot path needs the no-op-returns-false signal to avoid an infinite write loop.
name: stampLabelMembership

description: Starts the stable-Chrome system-load poll loop: runs pollSystemLoad then re-schedules every SYSTEM_POLL_INTERVAL_MS, idempotently (guards against a double timer). Defensively switches back to the chrome.processes listener if that richer API appears mid-session.
name: startSystemLoadPolling

description: Event guard that stops propagation on UrlField key events, keeping the global keydown handler from hijacking typing inside the field. Reproduced faithfully from the original.
name: stopProp

untestabilityReason.justification: single-expression wrapper over event.stopPropagation() — no branching or logic to test

description: Clears the system-load poll timer and resets it to null, ending the stable-Chrome fallback sampling loop (used on switch-to-processes and on a system-call failure).
name: stopSystemLoadPolling

description: Translates a drop index from the order a group card PAINTS its rows (open tabs first, via labelDisplayOrder) into an index in the stored urlKeys array: finds the key occupying that displayed slot and returns its stored position, so the row is inserted immediately before it. An index at or past the end -- an ambiguous drop, or the last slot -- appends, matching what the service worker does when it files a new member. Module-private to dragReducer and exercised through applyDrag, which is the contract worth pinning; a negative or non-numeric index also appends rather than throwing.
name: storageIndexForDisplayIndex

description: Converts quotes a word processor autocorrected back to straight ones. Applied last among the transport repairs and only after a strict parse has already failed, because curly quotes are perfectly legal inside a JSON string — a snapshot whose only curly quotes sit in a page title parses on the first pass and never reaches here.
name: straightenSmartQuotes

description: Unwraps a snapshot that arrived inside a markdown code fence, as it does whenever an export is pasted through a chat client or a markdown document. Returns null when there is no fence, so a healthy paste is never reported to the user as having been repaired.
name: stripCodeFence

description: Drops a comma sitting immediately before a closing brace or bracket — the classic hand-edit left behind by deleting the last group. String-aware, so a comma inside a page title is content rather than syntax, and a comma genuinely separating two members survives.
name: stripTrailingCommas

description: Slices leading or trailing prose away from around an otherwise intact snapshot, from the first structural character to the last. Returns null when the text is already just the snapshot.
name: stripWrapper

description: Subscribes to drag-start/drag-end transitions so a list can flush the storage updates it buffered mid-drag. Uses a listener set separate from the hover subscription so flipping one signal never wakes the other's subscribers.
name: subscribeDragActive

description: Subscribes a listener to cursor drop-hover changes and returns an unsubscribe function, letting each group card repaint independently as the cursor moves between groups.
name: subscribeDragHover

description: Builds the success result every parse pass returns, folding the shape-validation drop count together with any groups lost to salvage into one `lost` total. Both are the same fact to the user — groups that were in the file and did not come back — so the reporting layer should never have to know which pass discarded them.
name: succeed

description: Summarizes a stored per-URL processes record into the load readout a tab shows: average CPU and private-memory, a severity level (low/medium/high/excessive), and a bar width. Returns null when there is no sampled data so callers render nothing. Shared by the Url tab rows and the Load page LoadUrl cards (extracted from the inline copy that lived in Url).
name: summarizeProcessLoad

description: Whether chrome.storage.sync exists at all. Absent in unit tests that stub only storage.local and in any host predating the shim's sync support; degrading to local-only there preserves exactly the pre-sync behavior instead of throwing on chrome.storage.sync.set of undefined.
name: syncAvailable

description: Detects whether chrome.system.cpu and chrome.system.memory are both present, gating the stable-Chrome whole-browser load fallback that drives the gauge when chrome.processes is unavailable.
name: systemApiAvailable

description: Builds the per-url update record for a tab — resolving an empty object for invalid tabs and otherwise merging the stored url with fresh tab/process metadata via urlUpdates.
name: tabUpdates

description: Records a Chrome tab group's title keyed by its integer id in the worker's in-memory `groups` map, used to resolve a tab's label when its group changes.
name: trackGroup

description: The worker's single storage-write chokepoint. Routes each key to its owning area (labels -> sync, everything else -> local) and guards the sync path against quota and availability failures. Also COALESCES: a labels write byte-identical to the last one persisted is dropped, because labels now lives in sync, which caps writes at 120/minute — and recordInGroupTab runs per tab from groupTabs on every activeTabs change, so re-persisting an unchanged map would breach the quota within a minute of ordinary browsing. Dropping is safe by construction since identical content means storage already holds the value.
name: update

description: Queries all normal-window tabs and rebuilds the persisted `activeTabs` list (urlKey, pinned, groupId, timestamps, auto-closed state), debounced via waitingToUpdate, then writes it to chrome.storage.local.
name: updateActiveTabs

description: Accumulates a single process's cpu/network/privateMemory/jsMemoryAllocated/jsMemoryUsed into the running processTotals, treating missing metrics as 0.
name: updateTotals

description: Predicate for whether a urlKey is a deliberate, recorded member of a tab-group label. Centralizes the membership check shared by the auto-group ejection and recording paths; tolerates a missing label by returning false.
name: urlKeyIsMember

description: Merges a tab current title/favicon/groupId into a stored url record and accumulates rolling process metrics, normalizing running averages past a 100-sample window. Skips the live-tab title/favicon reassignment when the record has edited:true so a user-curated title/favicon is not clobbered on the next tracking tick.
name: urlUpdates

description: Predicate used by rankFavorites: true when a url record exists and has a non-empty string title, so favorite candidates without a renderable title are filtered out of the ranking.
name: usableTitle

description: Pure helper returning the largest single-bucket visit count across every favorite's daily AND weekly usage buckets, floored at 1. The Favorites View All page passes this as a common maximum to every row's UsageSparkline so bar heights are comparable across rows — a busy site reads visibly taller than a quiet one — instead of each chart self-scaling to its own busiest bucket. Uses bucketVisitsByDay and bucketVisitsByWeek.
name: usageMax

description: Owns the History page's data. Reads allUrls, autoClosed and labels plus each url record, dates every row via historyTimestamp, buckets it with bucketByDay against a now recomputed per load, colors it from label membership, and returns the rows sorted newest-first with undated rows last. Subscribes to chrome.storage.onChanged so the page stays live without a remount. Exposes reopen to open a row's url in a new tab, and deleteRow to delete it from history via deleteUrlFromHistory — deleteRow needs no local state surgery because the same onChanged listener re-loads on the resulting allUrls change, so the row disappears on its own. Returns rows, reopen and deleteRow.
name: useHistoryRows

description: React hook owning the degraded-sync banner state for any surface outside the Import / Export page, where the warning must be dismissible rather than permanently parked above the user's groups. Dismissal is deliberately PER-INCIDENT: it records the `at` of the status record being dismissed, and writeByArea only writes a new record when the status actually changes, so a dismissal holds while sync stays broken and lifts when sync recovers and then fails again. Returns `{status, dismiss}` with status nulled while dismissed.
name: useSyncStatus

untestabilityReason.justification: Reads chrome.storage through Chrome and subscribes to chrome.storage.onChanged; its behaviour is exercised end to end by the home-groups-survive-a-sync-fallback application scenario.

description: React hook owning the resolved light/dark theme. Resolves from three inputs: the saved themePreference storage key ['system' | 'light' | 'dark', default system], the live OS prefers-color-scheme tracked via matchMedia [dark fallback], and an in-memory temporary override set by the sun/moon toggle. Only the resolved value mirrors to the document element's data-theme attribute, which the CSS token layer keys off so the whole UI re-themes from one place. In system mode an OS day/night transition clears the override; a legacy theme:'light' migrates to a Day preference. Returns [theme, toggleTheme].
name: useTheme

description: Predicate that excludes empty and browser-internal tabs (chrome://, devtools://, chrome-extension://) from tracking.
name: validTab

description: Private helper in rankFavorites that resolves a url record's effective visit timestamps for scoring: it returns the record's own pruned visits when present, otherwise lazily seeds them from visitCount via seedVisitsFromCount so a legacy record still ranks, and returns an empty array when neither is available. Always returns a retention-bounded, length-capped ascending array via pruneVisits.
name: visitsFor

description: Writes an updates map to its keys' owning areas, guarding every sync write two ways sync can refuse one: an over-quota item is measured first and redirected to local, and a rejected write (signed out, sync disabled, throttled) is retried into local off chrome.runtime.lastError. Both record the outcome under syncStatus so a group mutation is never dropped and the degraded state is visible rather than silent. A SUCCESSFUL sync write additionally mirrors the value back into local, so an earlier fallback copy can never linger and leave the two areas holding different groups — mirroring rather than deleting, because migrateLabelsToSync keeps the local copy on purpose as a read-only net for the day sync is unavailable.
name: writeByArea
